source.title: Recent developments and open problems in the mathematical theory of viscoelasticity

trace.notes: Normalized the input as the zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/3945479 for document identifier 3945479. Local workflow shard metadata identifies the exact work as 'Recent developments and open problems in the mathematical theory of viscoelasticity', published in 1985, with no direct full-text links. Exact-title search confirmed the same chapter as Michael Renardy's contribution in the edited volume 'Viscoelasticity and Rheology', pages 345-360.

Failure mode: network_or_dns_failure plus metadata_only and paywalled_or_restricted. Local shell fetches could not resolve zbmath.org or api.zbmath.org from the execution sandbox. Browser/page-reader resolution of the exact zbMATH URL did not expose a readable record body or full-text artifact, so the zbMATH record was treated only as a bibliographic resolver.
evidence_refs: curl: Could not resolve host: api.zbmath.org

trace.notes: Bounded exact-work recovery used the zbMATH identifier, exact title, exact title plus PDF, the author name Michael Renardy, the MRC report number 2770, and the NTIS-style accession string AD A149 043/ADA149043. Recovered candidates were rejected because they exposed only metadata, catalog/table-of-contents entries, citation references, publication-list entries, or different works: the ScienceDirect book page marks the chapter as abstract-only/purchase access, Elsevier and bookseller pages are catalog records, Michael Renardy's vita is a publication list, the MRC bibliography PDF is only a bibliographic listing, and the SIAM page merely cites the chapter in a reference list.
No document map was produced because no readable exact-work PDF or full HTML source containing the chapter's open-problem statements was recovered.

The source-adequacy gate forbids extracting questions from zbMATH metadata, ScienceDirect abstract-only pages, publisher catalogs, book tables of contents, publication lists, citation references, search snippets, or related works. No candidates had verbatim open-problem evidence with page numbers or stable HTML locators from a readable primary source, so accepted remains empty.
